rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that each of several separately built items is then tested individually, with the build and test of each item following in a stated order, and the items are brought together only after their tests: Model each item's stated sequence (build, then test) as its own task pair inside a parallel branch, one branch per item, with each test as a separate task. Open the branches with a parallel split and close them with a parallel join before the step that brings the items together, so that this step starts only after every item has been built and tested. Model the test outcome of each item as an exclusive gateway: the successful outcome continues toward the joining step, and the unsuccessful outcome loops back to the redesign and rebuild activity for that item. Do not collapse the per-item builds and tests into one task, and do not place the joining step after a single branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that each of several separately built items is then tested individually, with the build and test of each item following in a stated order, and the items are brought together only after their tests

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one activity covers two or more independent checks or evaluations joined by 'and', and a later decision or step depends on all of them being completed: Model each stated check or evaluation as its own task, not as one combined task. Place a parallel (AND) split before these tasks so that all of them start, and close them with a parallel join before the decision or step that depends on their results. Label each task with that check's own wording from the description. Do not use an exclusive gateway for checks that must all complete.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that each of several items is produced and then checked on its own, and a later joint step may start only when all of these checks succeed, with failing items sent to a corrective path

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a number of items are each processed in turn, and an item that fails its check must be reworked before the process moves on: After the rework activity for a failed item, place an exclusive gateway that asks whether items remain to be processed. Route one flow back to the activity that processes the next item and another flow onward to the step that follows the item cycle once no items remain. Label the gateway with the description's own wording for the remaining-items question, and label the two flows with the outcomes the description gives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a number of items are each processed in turn, and an item that fails its check must be reworked before the process moves on

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a set of items (up to a stated number) is handled in parallel, with each item in its own branch that must finish before the process continues: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one branch per item being processed in parallel, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the shared continuation. Do not use an exclusive gateway for the fork or the join, and do not put decision conditions on the parallel branches. A stated limit on how many items run at once can be shown in the task or the description, not as a gateway condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a product is made of several parts, each part is produced and then checked on its own, and a later step follows only when every check has passed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a product is made of several components, each component is produced by an activity and then checked on its own, and a later assembly step is performed only if every check succeeds, with failed components sent back for rebuilding: Model one produce-then-check pair of tasks per component, each pair in its own branch. Start all component branches with a parallel (AND) split gateway and close them with a parallel (AND) join gateway. After the join, place an exclusive decision gateway on the overall check outcome: the success flow continues to the assembly step, and the failure flow returns to the rebuild task of the failed components. Do not model all components with one generic produce task and one generic check task, and do not use exclusive gateways for the split or the join.
